---
title: "I cannot choose a method"
last-reviewed: "2026-08-28"
---

## Start with the claim

Before comparing methods, write what you want to find out. Do you need to estimate a difference, explain an experience or test a prediction? That answer helps you choose what evidence to collect.

## Try this now

1. Connect the question to the evidence, design, sample or material, measures and analysis it needs.
2. Compare two or three methods you could realistically use.
3. Check their assumptions, access needs, expertise, participant burden, risks and time.
4. Test the most uncertain requirement with a small, affordable trial where permitted.
5. Take the comparison to a methods adviser. Record your provisional choice and what would make you revisit it.

## What to take when asking

Bring your question, the options table, any trial results and your recommendation. Point out what you're still unsure about.

## Stop or escalate

Pause if none of the options can answer the question safely and with the necessary approval. Having the software, or finding a paper that used it, doesn't establish that a method fits your study.

## You are moving again when

You've chosen a method for reasons you can explain and agreed which assumptions need testing, which approvals you need and when to reconsider.

Use the [method-options table](../templates/method-options.qmd) and [method decision record](../templates/method-decision.qmd).
